problem_text:
A city planner must select infrastructure projects to maximize total community benefit while staying within the annual budget allocation.

The candidate projects are:
* Project 1: cost 6 million, benefit 240 units
* Project 2: cost 19 million, benefit 169 units
* Project 3: cost 32 million, benefit 202 units
* Project 4: cost 18 million, benefit 123 units
* Project 5: cost 44 million, benefit 296 units
* Project 6: cost 24 million, benefit 281 units
* Project 7: cost 39 million, benefit 65 units
* Project 8: cost 41 million, benefit 176 units
* Project 9: cost 26 million, benefit 199 units
* Project 10: cost 8 million, benefit 283 units
* Project 11: cost 50 million, benefit 84 units
* Project 12: cost 40 million, benefit 253 units
* Project 13: cost 40 million, benefit 206 units
* Project 14: cost 34 million, benefit 189 units
* Project 15: cost 18 million, benefit 283 units
* Project 16: cost 10 million, benefit 79 units
* Project 17: cost 5 million, benefit 88 units
* Project 18: cost 6 million, benefit 141 units
* Project 19: cost 3 million, benefit 122 units
* Project 20: cost 42 million, benefit 268 units
* Project 21: cost 23 million, benefit 209 units
* Project 22: cost 36 million, benefit 188 units
* Project 23: cost 48 million, benefit 64 units
* Project 24: cost 45 million, benefit 267 units
* Project 25: cost 46 million, benefit 250 units
* Project 26: cost 2 million, benefit 113 units

Furthermore, due to overlapping service areas, exactly one of Project 1 and Project 2 can be approved.

If Project 3 is approved, it mandates an associated environmental mitigation fund that reduces the effective annual budget by 10 million.
The total available budget for the fiscal year is 493 million. The planner must determine the optimal portfolio of projects to fund.
